html:
The Battle of Blenheim was fought on 13 August 1704 at the village of Blindheim on the Danube in Bavaria, southern Germany. An allied army under the English Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy destroyed a French and Bavarian army under Marshal Tallard.

It was part of the War of the Spanish Succession. France and Bavaria planned to march on Vienna and knock the Habsburg emperor out of the war. To stop them, Marlborough marched his army about 400 km from the Low Countries to the Danube in five weeks and joined Eugene. They attacked a slightly larger army in a strong position. Tallard had packed much of his infantry into Blenheim village. Marlborough pinned it there, then broke through the weak French centre with cavalry. Tallard was captured, and about 30,000 of his men were killed, wounded or taken.

Vienna was saved and Bavaria was knocked out of the war. It was the first great defeat of Louis XIV's armies in two generations, and it ended the belief that France could not be beaten on land. A grateful queen and parliament built Blenheim Palace for Marlborough.
